entities.name: Tuberculosis
entities.description: Chronic granulomatous infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, transmitted airborne via droplet nuclei, primarily affecting pulmonary parenchyma with characteristic cavitation, but capable of extrapulmonary dissemination.

entities.name: Airborne Inhalation of Droplet Nuclei in Poorly Ventilated Spaces
entities.description: Exclusively airborne transmission via microscopic droplet nuclei (1–5 µm) suspended in ambient air from infectious coughs or sneezes, heavily exacerbated by prolonged indoor contact in crowded, poorly ventilated environments such as prisons, homeless shelters, and refugee camps.

entities.name: Advanced HIV/AIDS Immunosuppression
entities.description: Most potent host risk factor (12-fold increased risk of active disease; leading cause of HIV-associated mortality), driving rapid reactivation of latent infection or accelerated progression of primary disease due to depleted CD4+ T-cell-mediated immunity.

entities.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Chronic Hyperglycemia
entities.description: Major host comorbidity that triples the lifetime risk of active tuberculosis reactivation due to impaired alveolar macrophage phagocytosis, defective chemotaxis, and blunted cell-mediated immune responses.

entities.name: Silicosis and Occupational Dust Inhalation
entities.description: Occupational exposure causing macrophage lysis and pulmonary fibrosis, producing up to a 30-fold increased lifetime susceptibility to pulmonary tuberculosis (silicotuberculosis).

entities.name: High-Burden Endemic Geography in South-East Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa
entities.description: Residency or prolonged travel in countries with extreme tuberculosis incidence and prevalence (such as India, Indonesia, China, the Philippines, Pakistan, Nigeria, and South Africa), accounting for over 80% of global cases.

entities.name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Complex
entities.description: Obligate aerobic, slow-growing, acid-fast bacillus with a lipid-rich, mycolic-acid-dense cell wall that resists Gram staining, acid-alcohol decolorization, and intracellular macrophage destruction.

entities.name: Chronic Productive Cough Exceeding 3 Weeks with Hemoptysis
entities.description: Indolent cough lasting >2–3 weeks progressing from dry irritation to purulent or blood-streaked sputum, potentially escalating to life-threatening Rasmussen aneurysm rupture within cavitary lesions.

entities.name: Drenching Night Sweats with Profound Cachectic Weight Loss
entities.description: Classic systemic constitutional B-symptom triad comprising soaking nocturnal diaphoresis requiring change of clothing, evening low-grade fever spikes, and progressive wasting consumption.

entities.name: Matted Cervical Lymphadenopathy with Cold Abscess Formation
entities.description: Scrofula presentation featuring firm, matted, non-tender cervical or supraclavicular lymph node enlargement that softens into fluctuant cold abscesses with chronic fistulous drainage.

entities.name: Thoracolumbar Vertebral Gibbus Deformity with Cold Psoas Abscess
entities.description: Pott disease presentation characterized by localized spinal pain, anterior vertebral body collapse causing acute angular kyphosis (gibbus deformity), and tracking retroperitoneal cold psoas abscesses.

entities.name: Apical and Posterior Upper Lobe Cavitary Infiltrates on Chest Radiography
entities.description: Heterogeneous patchy consolidation and thick-walled cavitary lesions localized to the apical/posterior segments of the upper lobes or superior segments of lower lobes, often surrounded by tree-in-bud nodular satellite opacities.

entities.name: Diffuse Bilateral 1-2 mm Micronodular Opacities on Chest Radiography
entities.description: Classic 'millet seed' pattern of uniform, 1–2 mm discrete micronodules evenly distributed throughout both lungs from apex to base, reflecting acute hematogenous miliary dissemination.

entities.name: Acid-Fast Bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen or Auramine-O Sputum Microscopy
entities.description: Immediate admission microscopical visualization of bright red or glowing rod-shaped acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen or auramine-O fluorochrome stained sputum smears.

entities.name: Rapid Sputum Cartridge NAAT Detection of MTB Complex and rpoB Resistance
entities.description: Rapid cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification (Xpert MTB/RIF) providing bacteriological confirmation of M. tuberculosis DNA and detecting mutations in the rpoB gene within 2 hours directly from sputum.

entities.name: Normocytic Anemia with Reactive Thrombocytosis and Extreme ESR Elevation
entities.description: Admission hematology showing normocytic normochromic anemia (Hb 8–11 g/dL), normal or mildly elevated WBC without marked leukocytosis, elevated platelets (400,000–600,000/µL), and marked ESR elevation (>60–100 mm/h).

entities.name: Polyserositis and Splenic Microabscesses on Bedside FASH Ultrasound
entities.description: Focused Assessment with Sonography for HIV-associated TB (FASH) identifying pericardial effusion, pleural fluid, ascites, and abdominal lymphadenopathy (>1.5 cm) or hypoechoic splenic microabscesses at triage.

entities.name: Hyperacute Febrile Respiratory Distress Evolving Within 48-72 Hours
entities.description: Hyperacute onset of fever, rigors, and dyspnea developing in under 48 to 72 hours, which strongly points toward acute pyogenic bacterial community-acquired pneumonia rather than indolent tuberculosis.

entities.name: Marked Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia Exceeding 15 Percent
entities.description: Absolute eosinophil count >1,500/µL or eosinophil fraction >15–30%, which is virtually never seen in active pulmonary tuberculosis and indicates parasitic lung flukes (Paragonimiasis) or allergic/fungal pulmonary disease.

entities.name: Complete Radiographic Resolution Within 5-7 Days of Beta-Lactam Monotherapy
entities.description: Rapid clinical defervescence and near-total radiological resolution of pulmonary consolidation within 5 to 7 days of treatment with standard beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g., amoxicillin, ceftriaxone).

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis Exceeding 15000 per Microliter with Severe Left Shift
entities.description: Pronounced peripheral leukocytosis (WBC >15,000–30,000/µL) with bandemia >15% and hyperacute procalcitonin elevation, which is distinctly atypical for uncomplicated active tuberculosis and indicates acute pyogenic sepsis or melioidosis.

entities.name: Melioidosis
entities.description: Severe tropical infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei presenting with upper-lobe cavitary pneumonia and hemoptysis in endemic regions of Southeast Asia and Northern Australia.

entities.name: Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Endemic lung fluke infection caused by Paragonimus westermani contracted through ingestion of raw or undercooked freshwater crabs/crayfish, mimicking pulmonary TB with chronic cough and hemoptysis.

entities.name: Bronchogenic Carcinoma
entities.description: Primary pulmonary malignancy occurring in older smokers presenting with chronic cough, hemoptysis, cachexia, and cavitary or nodular lung lesions.

entities.name: Paracoccidioidomycosis
entities.description: Endemic South American systemic mycosis caused by Paracoccidioides brasiliensis presenting with chronic cavitary lung disease, lymphadenopathy, and mucosal ulcerations.

entities.name: Standard First-Line 4-Drug Regimen (Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol)
entities.description: WHO-standardized short-course antitubercular therapy (RIPE) comprising a 2-month intensive phase (RHZE) followed by a 4-month continuation phase (RH), yielding clinical defervescence within 2–4 weeks and sputum smear conversion by month 2.

entities.name: Mandatory Pyridoxine Co-Administration to Prevent Isoniazid Neurotoxicity
entities.description: Mandatory daily supplementation with Vitamin B6 (25–50 mg daily) to prevent dose-dependent isoniazid-induced peripheral sensory neuropathy and central neurotoxicity.

entities.name: Fluoroquinolone-Induced Transient Symptomatic Masking Hazard
entities.description: Partial, transient clinical and radiographic improvement following empirical respiratory fluoroquinolone monotherapy (e.g., levofloxacin, moxifloxacin) due to inherent anti-mycobacterial activity, creating hazardous diagnostic delays.

entities.name: Intrinsic Resistance to Broad-Spectrum Beta-Lactam and Standard Cephalosporin Monotherapy
entities.description: Intrinsic therapeutic refractoriness to standard aminopenicillins, first-to-fourth generation cephalosporins, and macrolides due to robust bacterial beta-lactamases and the impermeable mycolic acid cell envelope.

entities.name: Novel 6-Month All-Oral BPaLM Regimen for Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis
entities.description: WHO-recommended 6-month all-oral regimen consisting of Bedaquiline, Pretomanid, Linezolid, and Moxifloxacin (BPaLM) for rifampicin-resistant and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB).

relationships.target: Airborne Inhalation of Droplet Nuclei in Poorly Ventilated Spaces
relationships.keywords: TRANSMITTED_BY, droplet nuclei, airborne aerosol, inhalation, poorly ventilated indoor spaces
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Acquired exclusively via inhalation of aerosolized 1–5 µm droplet nuclei expelled by active infectious pulmonary cases, suspended in stagnant ambient air.

relationships.target: Advanced HIV/AIDS Immunosuppression
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, host susceptibility, CD4 immunosuppression, HIV coinfection, cellular immunity failure
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Severely impaired cell-mediated immunity in HIV/AIDS is the most potent global host risk factor, multiplying active disease reactivation risk by 12-fold.

relationships.target: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Chronic Hyperglycemia
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, host metabolic comorbidity, diabetes mellitus, macrophage dysfunction, reactivation
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Chronic hyperglycemia triples the risk of latent tuberculosis reactivation through impaired alveolar macrophage chemotaxis and blunted antigen presentation.

relationships.target: Silicosis and Occupational Dust Inhalation
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, occupational hazard, silica dust, macrophage lysis, silicotuberculosis
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Chronic occupational inhalation of crystalline silica destroys alveolar macrophages and elevates active tuberculosis risk up to 30-fold.

relationships.target: High-Burden Endemic Geography in South-East Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, geographic endemicity, high-burden settings, regional reservoir, transmission intensity
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Exposure or prolonged residence within hyperendemic regions of South-East Asia, the Western Pacific, or sub-Saharan Africa represents the primary epidemiological risk pool.

relationships.target: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Complex
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, etiologic agent, acid fast bacillus, mycolic acid cell wall, obligate aerobe
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, an obligate aerobe whose lipid-dense mycolic acid cell wall confers acid-fastness and intracellular persistence.

relationships.target: Chronic Productive Cough Exceeding 3 Weeks with Hemoptysis
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, cardinal sign, chronic hemoptysis, Rasmussen aneurysm
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Indolent cough lasting >3 weeks with blood-streaked sputum or life-threatening Rasmussen aneurysm hemoptysis reflects progressive bronchial ulceration and cavitary necrosis.

relationships.target: Drenching Night Sweats with Profound Cachectic Weight Loss
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, constitutional B-symptoms, drenching diaphoresis, consumption
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Subacute wasting cachexia accompanied by evening fever spikes and drenching nocturnal sweats represents the classic constitutional hallmark of active tuberculosis.

relationships.target: Matted Cervical Lymphadenopathy with Cold Abscess Formation
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, scrofula, tuberculous lymphadenitis, cold abscess
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Painless, firm, matted cervical or supraclavicular lymph node chains breaking down into cold abscesses and chronically draining fistulae represent the cardinal sign of scrofula.

relationships.target: Thoracolumbar Vertebral Gibbus Deformity with Cold Psoas Abscess
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, Pott disease, tuberculous spondylitis, gibbus deformity
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Sharp angular thoracolumbar kyphosis (gibbus) resulting from anterior vertebral body destruction with tracking cold psoas abscess is pathognomonic for skeletal tuberculosis.

relationships.target: Apical and Posterior Upper Lobe Cavitary Infiltrates on Chest Radiography
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, chest radiography, apical cavitary lesion, upper lobe infiltrates, tree in bud
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Plain admission chest radiograph shows patchy consolidation, tree-in-bud nodular satellite opacities, and thick-walled cavitary lesions localized to the apical/posterior upper lobes.

relationships.target: Diffuse Bilateral 1-2 mm Micronodular Opacities on Chest Radiography
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, miliary tuberculosis, micronodular interstitial pattern, millet seed appearance
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Uniform, diffuse 1–2 mm micronodular opacities evenly scattered from lung apices to bases on admission chest radiography reflect acute hematogenous miliary dissemination.

relationships.target: Acid-Fast Bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen or Auramine-O Sputum Microscopy
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, acid fast bacilli, Ziehl Neelsen smear, auramine O fluorescence, microscopic hallmark
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Direct admission sputum microscopy demonstrates bright red rods on Ziehl-Neelsen staining or glowing fluorescing rods under auramine-O microscopy.

relationships.target: Rapid Sputum Cartridge NAAT Detection of MTB Complex and rpoB Resistance
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, GeneXpert MTB/RIF, cartridge molecular assay, rpoB resistance, rapid admission NAAT
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Rapid cartridge-based automated NAAT (Xpert MTB/RIF) directly identifies M. tuberculosis complex DNA and detects rpoB rifampicin resistance mutations within 2 hours.

relationships.target: Normocytic Anemia with Reactive Thrombocytosis and Extreme ESR Elevation
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, anemia of chronic disease, normal WBC, reactive thrombocytosis, extreme ESR elevation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission laboratory profile demonstrates normocytic anemia (Hb 8-11 g/dL), normal or mildly elevated WBC, reactive thrombocytosis (400-600k/µL), and ESR markedly elevated >60-100 mm/h.

relationships.target: Polyserositis and Splenic Microabscesses on Bedside FASH Ultrasound
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, bedside ultrasound, FASH protocol, pericardial effusion, abdominal lymphadenopathy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Point-of-care ultrasound under the FASH protocol identifies pericardial effusion, pleural fluid, retroperitoneal/mesenteric lymphadenopathy (>1.5 cm), and hypoechoic splenic microabscesses at triage.

relationships.target: Hyperacute Febrile Respiratory Distress Evolving Within 48-72 Hours
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, hyperacute onset, temporal threshold
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Hyperacute onset of toxic fever and respiratory distress evolving within <48–72 hours strongly excludes uncomplicated tuberculosis, which inherently follows an insidious multi-week course.

relationships.target: Marked Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia Exceeding 15 Percent
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, peripheral eosinophilia, parasitic differentiation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] High-grade peripheral blood eosinophilia (>1,500/µL or >15–30%) strongly rules out pulmonary tuberculosis, pointing instead to parasitic fluke infestations or allergic bronchopulmonary disorders.

relationships.target: Complete Radiographic Resolution Within 5-7 Days of Beta-Lactam Monotherapy
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, beta lactam response, rapid clearing
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid clinical resolution and complete radiological clearance of pulmonary infiltrates within 5–7 days of standard beta-lactam therapy rules out mycobacterial infection.

relationships.target: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis Exceeding 15000 per Microliter with Severe Left Shift
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, leukocytosis threshold, toxic bandemia
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Profound neutrophilic leukocytosis (>15,000–30,000/µL) with toxic bandemia >15% is distinctly atypical for uncomplicated tuberculosis and points toward acute pyogenic sepsis or melioidosis.

relationships.target: Melioidosis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, Burkholderia pseudomallei, acute sepsis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Melioidosis presents with acute fulminant toxicity (<1–2 weeks), marked leukocytosis (>15,000/µL), and splenic honeycomb microabscesses primarily in diabetics; Tuberculosis presents with insidious progression (>3 weeks), normal/mild WBC, positive AFB/GeneXpert, and response to RIPE.

relationships.target: Paragonimiasis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, lung fluke, raw crustacean ingestion, eosinophilia
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Paragonimiasis presents with chronic cough, rusty-brown sputum, ingestion of raw freshwater crabs/crayfish, and marked peripheral eosinophilia (>15–30%); Tuberculosis lacks eosinophilia and reveals acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear microscopy.

relationships.target: Bronchogenic Carcinoma
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, pulmonary malignancy, cavitary mass
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Bronchogenic carcinoma presents in older smokers with irregular, eccentrically excavated thick-walled cavities lacking tree-in-bud satellites, negative AFB/GeneXpert, and malignant cytology on bronchoscopy.

relationships.target: Paracoccidioidomycosis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, endemic mycosis, mucosal ulceration, pilot wheel
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Paracoccidioidomycosis features mulberry-like ulcerative stomatitis in the oropharynx, marked cervical adenopathy, and pilot's wheel budding yeast cells on histology; Tuberculosis lacks oral mulberry ulcerations and yields acid-fast bacilli.

relationships.target: Standard First-Line 4-Drug Regimen (Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol)
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, RIPE regimen, first-line antitubercular therapy, defervescence timeline, sputum smear conversion
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Shows systematic clinical defervescence, cessation of nocturnal diaphoresis, and weight gain within 2–4 weeks of initiating 4-drug RIPE therapy, with sputum conversion to negative by month 2.

relationships.target: Mandatory Pyridoxine Co-Administration to Prevent Isoniazid Neurotoxicity
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, pyridoxine supplementation, vitamin B6, isoniazid prophylaxis, neuroprotection
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Requires mandatory co-administration of pyridoxine (vitamin B6, 25–50 mg daily) alongside isoniazid to prevent disabling dose-dependent peripheral sensory neuropathy.

relationships.target: Fluoroquinolone-Induced Transient Symptomatic Masking Hazard
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, fluoroquinolone masking, empirical quinolone delay, temporary defervescence
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Exhibits transient, deceptive symptomatic improvement upon empirical respiratory fluoroquinolone therapy (e.g., levofloxacin, moxifloxacin), which dangerously masks active tuberculosis and delays definitive therapy.

relationships.target: Intrinsic Resistance to Broad-Spectrum Beta-Lactam and Standard Cephalosporin Monotherapy
relationships.keywords: INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO, antibiotic failure, intrinsic resistance, beta-lactamase BlaC, cephalosporin refractoriness
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Intrinsically refractory to standard aminopenicillins and first-through-fourth generation cephalosporins due to constitutive BlaC beta-lactamase production and impermeable mycolic acid cell envelope.

relationships.target: Novel 6-Month All-Oral BPaLM Regimen for Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, MDR-TB, drug-resistant tuberculosis, BPaLM regimen, all-oral short course
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Multidrug-resistant and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis strains respond to the WHO-prioritized 6-month all-oral BPaLM regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, and moxifloxacin).
